messages:
infra-bot: ALERT: region=us-east-3 | metric=ECC_CORRECTED_RATE | scope=rack12-rack15 | value=spike above 95th percentile. Auto-drain policy triggered. Observed capacity drop ~12% (560 -> 493 GPUs). Grafana: https://grafana.redwood/orgs/1/d/ops/gpu-health?orgId=1

Dmitri: seeing the same. Also Xid 79 and NVLINK peer-reset messages in syslogs for gpu-node-ue3-r12-03. Posting a couple of sample lines:```kernel: nouveau 0000:af:00.0: nvlink peer reset detected
kern: nvidia: Xid (79) at 0x4f7c drawer```

Amy: confirmed. Prober heartbeats started lagging ~15s before the drain events. Telemetry aggregation shows 3 telemetry gaps per host in the last 10m.

Raj: hypothesis: telemetry misreads + intermittent NVLINK errors -> high corrected ECC counts because reads are reissued. Could be driver/kernel timing regression. Any recent driver/kernel rollouts in us-east-3?

Dmitri: we rolled kernel 6.2.18 -> 6.2.21 two nights ago on a subset (racks 10-16). Can we correlate nodes that got the kernel update?

Amy: running quick query now against configsvc: `select host, kernel_version from inventory where rack in (12,13,14,15)`

Amy: results: 80% of affected hosts are on 6.2.21. Non-affected racks still on 6.2.18.

Oncall-Mike: @dmitri @amy I'm on it. I will start triage runbook step 1: increase prober timeout and restart prober on two canary nodes, then watch metrics for 10m. If NVLINK resets continue, we'll evict and reprovision nodes.

Dmitri: also please disable auto-drain for the next 30m for group=canary to avoid mass churn while we confirm cause -> `infractl policy set auto_drain=false --group canary --ttl 30m`

Infra-bot: action logged: infractl run by oncall-mike, ticket INF-7891 created.

Oncall-Mike: restarted gpu-prober on gpu-node-ue3-r12-03 and gpu-node-ue3-r13-02: `systemctl restart gpu-prober` -> prober back up, heartbeat interval now stable at 2s. Waiting on ECC metric to normalize (10m window).

Raj: I pulled NVMe and kernel logs. There's a pattern: `nvlink_peer_timeout` followed by `ECC_corrected++` then Xid 79 a few seconds later. Looks like link-level retransmit flood. Could also be cabling/firmware. Any firmware rollouts on NVLINK fabric?

Amy: no firmware rollouts in last 30d. Only kernel + driver. Driver version on nodes: 525.85. We did a staged driver bump to 530.x on a different cohort last week, not these.

Dmitri: try rolling back kernel on one node to 6.2.18 and observe. If it is kernel-driven, rollback should stop the nvlink resets. Can we repro on a spare node?

Amy: spinning up a spare node in us-east-3 now and applying 6.2.21 to it to attempt repro locally (we want to see the reverse).

Zoe: tagging for capacity: we should move lower-priority batch jobs to dedicated-reserve-ord to avoid customer impact. That adds extra cost short-term but keeps SLOs. Estimated delta cost ~$8k/day for the burst.

Dmitri: 👍 do it. Amy, please start migration for non-prod and batch.

Amy: kicked off migration plan, moving ~40% of batch queue to ded-reserve-ord. `jobs migrate --label batch --target ded-reserve-ord --grace 60s`

Infra-bot: telemetry: ECC spike started 2026-03-18T02:12:30Z, peak window 02:20-02:28Z. Auto-drains executed for 27 hosts.

Oncall-Mike: after restarting prober + disabling auto-drain for canary, ECC rates on the canary hosts fell ~60% within 8m, but other nodes still noisy. I'm starting manual eviction+replace for nodes with >500 corrected ECC in last hour per runbook step 4.

Raj: I'm leaning driver/kernel. If rollback on a test node fixes it, we should schedule a targeted rollback for affected racks and then open a driver/kernel investigation with infra-kernel team.

Amy: rollback complete on test node (6.2.21 -> 6.2.18). Observed within 5m: nvlink resets stopped and Xid count zeroed. Re-running telemetry check.

Dmitri: that pretty strongly implicates kernel 6.2.21. Patch lane: pin kernel for hosts in racks 12-15 to 6.2.18 and coordinate with infra-kernel for a hotfix.

Zoe: cost note: keeping dedicated extra capacity and node replacements will increase monthly burn. Approving transient spend for customer SLO safety.

Amy: started automated pin via orchestration: `orchestrator set kernel_version=6.2.18 --filter rack in (12,13,14,15)` -> job enqueued. Rolling driver restarts scheduled to avoid mass reboots.

Oncall-Mike: replacing 12 of the worst nodes now (those that already triggered drain). Replacement progressing: 4/12 completed. No further customer-visible impact so far.

Infra-bot: update: capacity now at 98% (548/560); ECC corrected rate trending down to baseline. Ticket INF-7891 updated with mitigation steps and rollback proof-of-fix.

Dmitri: good work. Post-incident actions: 1) rollback kernel in affected racks, 2) run full NVLINK stress test on 6.2.21 in staging with telemetry profiler, 3) create a postmortem with timeline and cost delta, 4) consider turning on a driver-level NVLINK health monitor to pre-empt.

Zoe: please include cost delta estimate for the migration/replacement in the postmortem. I flagged finance.

Sara: thumbs up from support: customer impact minimal, some jobs delayed. Nice comms. :thumbsup:

Dmitri: closing thread for active mitigation. We will keep monitoring for 6h before declaring fully resolved. Assigning follow-up P0 to Raj for root cause analysis and Amy for remediation rollout.

amy: will write a short runbook addendum for kernel pin and driver checks.

raj: starting RCA now, will include kernel-client interactions and telemetry gap analysis.

infra-bot: Incident mitigation in progress, severity lowered to SEV-2. Follow-up ticket INF-7892 created for postmortem.

Dmitri: last update: capacity stable, errors down to baseline. Leaving on-call note and schedule postmortem for 2026-03-19 16:00 UTC.
